topics.label: Why Test
topics.desc: The case for automated tests: catching regressions, enabling safe refactoring, documenting intent, and shipping faster with confidence rather than relying on manual click-through QA.

topics.label: Test Pyramid
topics.desc: Mike Cohn's heuristic favoring many fast unit tests, fewer integration tests, and a thin layer of slow end-to-end tests to balance speed, cost, and confidence.

topics.label: Testing Trophy
topics.desc: Kent C. Dodds's alternative to the pyramid that weights integration tests most heavily, atop a base of static analysis, arguing they give the best confidence-per-effort.

topics.label: Test Levels
topics.desc: The spectrum from unit to integration to end-to-end, each verifying a wider slice of the system, trading isolation and speed for realism and broader coverage.

topics.label: Arrange-Act-Assert
topics.desc: The three-phase structure for a readable test: set up state, exercise the code under test, then assert outcomes, mirrored by the Given-When-Then phrasing used in BDD.

topics.label: Test Coverage
topics.desc: The percentage of code exercised by tests (line, branch, statement), measured by tools like Istanbul, useful as a gap finder but a misleading proxy for real quality.

topics.label: Regression Testing
topics.desc: Re-running existing tests after changes to ensure previously working features still work, plus smoke tests as a fast go/no-go sanity check on critical paths.

topics.label: Test Runners
topics.desc: The engine that discovers test files, executes them, isolates state, and reports results, such as Jest, Vitest, Mocha, pytest, or the JUnit Platform launcher.

topics.label: Jest
topics.desc: Meta's batteries-included JavaScript framework bundling a runner, expect-style matchers, mocking, snapshots, and coverage, long the default for React and Node testing.

topics.label: Vitest
topics.desc: A Vite-native test framework with a Jest-compatible API, fast ESM and TypeScript support, watch mode, and in-source testing, increasingly the modern default.

topics.label: pytest & JUnit
topics.desc: Python's pytest with plain-assert tests, fixtures, and parametrization, plus Java's JUnit whose annotations defined the xUnit model, the dominant unit frameworks beyond JavaScript's.

topics.label: Matchers & Assertions
topics.desc: The expressive assertion vocabulary (toEqual, toContain, toThrow, toHaveBeenCalled) that decides pass or fail and yields clear failure messages in Jest, Vitest, and Chai.

topics.label: Parameterized Tests
topics.desc: Running one test body over many input and expected-output cases via table-driven helpers like Jest's test.each, pytest.mark.parametrize, or JUnit's @ParameterizedTest.

topics.label: Snapshot Testing
topics.desc: Serializing output and committing it as a baseline that future runs diff against, handy for UI and config but prone to rubber-stamped updates if reviewed carelessly.

topics.label: Test Doubles
topics.desc: Gerard Meszaros's umbrella term for stand-ins replacing real collaborators, comprising dummies, stubs (canned responses), spies (record calls), mocks, and fakes.

topics.label: Mocks
topics.desc: Programmable doubles with preset expectations that verify interactions, asserting specific methods were called with given arguments the right number of times, via Sinon or jest.fn.

topics.label: Fakes & Fixtures
topics.desc: Lightweight working stand-ins like an in-memory repository or fake clock, plus reusable setup and canned data managed by pytest fixtures or beforeEach hooks.

topics.label: DI for Tests
topics.desc: Injecting dependencies through constructors or parameters rather than hardcoding them, so tests can swap in doubles, the design lever that makes code testable.

topics.label: Mocking Modules & HTTP
topics.desc: Replacing imports and intercepting network calls in tests using jest.mock, MSW request handlers, or nock, so suites run offline and deterministically.

topics.label: Over-Mocking Pitfalls
topics.desc: The trap of mocking so heavily that tests verify implementation details and pass while the real system breaks, coupling tests to internals and eroding their value.

topics.label: Integration Scope
topics.desc: Testing how multiple units collaborate across real boundaries like a service and its database or two modules, catching wiring and contract bugs that unit tests miss.

topics.label: API & Route Testing
topics.desc: Driving HTTP endpoints through the real app stack and asserting status, headers, and body, using Supertest for Node or FastAPI's TestClient and httpx in Python.

topics.label: Database Testing
topics.desc: Exercising real queries, migrations, and transactions against an actual or in-memory database engine to validate schema and persistence logic that mocks would hide.

topics.label: Test Containers
topics.desc: Spinning up disposable, production-like dependencies in Docker per test run via Testcontainers, giving real Postgres, Redis, or Kafka without shared environments.

topics.label: Seeding Test Data
topics.desc: Populating a test database with known rows via fixtures, factories, or seed scripts, then resetting between tests through truncation or transaction rollback.

topics.label: Test Isolation
topics.desc: Keeping tests independent so order and shared state never cause leaks, achieved with per-test transactions, fresh schemas, or cleanup hooks to prevent cross-contamination.

topics.label: Browser Automation
topics.desc: Programmatically driving a real browser to click, type, and navigate as a user would, the foundation beneath every end-to-end tool from Selenium to Playwright.

topics.label: Playwright
topics.desc: Microsoft's modern E2E framework driving Chromium, Firefox, and WebKit with auto-waiting, network interception, parallel execution, and built-in tracing.

topics.label: Cypress
topics.desc: A developer-friendly E2E tool running in the browser with time-travel debugging, automatic retries, and a live runner, popular for its DX despite single-tab limits.

topics.label: Selenium & Puppeteer
topics.desc: The long-standing WebDriver standard automating any browser across languages, and Google's Puppeteer driving Chrome via DevTools for automation and scraping.

topics.label: Page Object Model
topics.desc: A pattern wrapping each page's selectors and actions behind a reusable class so E2E tests read at the business level and survive UI markup changes with one edit.

topics.label: E2E Flakiness & Cross-Browser
topics.desc: Taming nondeterministic failures from timing and network races with auto-waiting and stable selectors, plus verifying behavior across browsers on grids like BrowserStack.

topics.label: Testing Library
topics.desc: A family (React, Vue, DOM) that queries rendered UI by accessible role and text rather than internals, on the philosophy that tests resembling real usage give more confidence.

topics.label: Component Testing
topics.desc: Rendering a single UI component in isolation and asserting its markup and behavior, via Testing Library, Cypress Component Testing, or Playwright's component runner.

topics.label: User-Event Simulation
topics.desc: Firing realistic interactions like typing, clicking, and tabbing through the user-event library, which dispatches the full event sequences a real person would trigger.

topics.label: Visual Regression
topics.desc: Catching unintended UI changes by diffing rendered screenshots against approved baselines using tools like Chromatic, Percy, or Playwright's snapshot comparison.

topics.label: Storybook Interaction Tests
topics.desc: Writing play functions on Storybook stories to script and assert component interactions, reusing isolated component states as both living documentation and tests.

topics.label: Accessibility Testing
topics.desc: Automatically auditing rendered UI for WCAG violations like missing labels or poor contrast using axe-core, jest-axe, or Lighthouse, complementing manual checks.

topics.label: TDD
topics.desc: Test-Driven Development's red-green-refactor loop: write a failing test, make it pass minimally, then clean up, driving design and ensuring every line is tested.

topics.label: BDD
topics.desc: Behavior-Driven Development expressing requirements as Given-When-Then scenarios in Gherkin, executable via Cucumber or SpecFlow to align developers and stakeholders.

topics.label: Tests in CI
topics.desc: Running the suite automatically on every push and pull request through GitHub Actions or similar, blocking merges on failures to keep the main branch always green.

topics.label: Flaky-Test Management
topics.desc: Systematically detecting, quarantining, and fixing intermittently failing tests so they neither block deploys nor train teams to ignore red builds.

topics.label: Test Data Management
topics.desc: Generating and maintaining realistic, isolated test data with factories like Faker or factory_bot, builders, and anonymized datasets, while avoiding shared mutable state.

topics.label: Contract Testing
topics.desc: Verifying that services agree on request and response shapes by testing each side against a shared contract, often consumer-driven with Pact, catching breaks before integration.

topics.label: Mutation Testing
topics.desc: Measuring test-suite strength by injecting small code mutations and checking whether tests catch them, via Stryker or PIT, exposing weak assertions that coverage misses.

topics.label: Static Analysis
topics.desc: Inspecting source without running it to surface bugs, smells, and security issues, spanning linters, type checkers, and platforms like SonarQube and CodeQL.

topics.label: Type Checking
topics.desc: Catching type errors before runtime with compilers and checkers like the TypeScript tsc, mypy, or Pyright, eliminating a whole class of defects no test would need.

topics.label: Linters as Quality Gates
topics.desc: Enforcing code standards and catching error-prone patterns with ESLint or Ruff, wired into CI and pre-commit hooks to fail builds on violations.

topics.label: Coverage Tools
topics.desc: Instrumenting code to report executed lines and branches via Istanbul, c8, or coverage.py, then tracking trends and PR diffs through Codecov or Coveralls.

topics.label: SonarQube & Complexity
topics.desc: A code-quality platform aggregating bugs, duplication, and complexity metrics like cyclomatic and cognitive scores into a dashboard with a pass/fail quality gate.

topics.label: Quality Gates in CI
topics.desc: Automated thresholds on coverage, lint, types, and complexity that must pass before merge, turning quality standards into enforced, non-negotiable pipeline checks.
